comments.body:
As I'm one of the potential users of this, I can probably comment on the interface. I believe this would solve my use case (or make it significantly easier to solve, the `is_eof` was the crucial part and the number of bytes could be extracted by using a custom iterator ‒ possible, but complex and tedious).

One question, though. If I hit the EOF, I can take the remainder of the data, append more to it and create a new deserializer on top of it (obviously). But is there a way to reuse the existing one? Or is the deserializer lightweight enough so the creation of a new one doesn't matter?

Constructing a deserializer is lightweight enough.

In the future I see this being used in something like [`tokio-serde-json`](https://github.com/carllerche/tokio-serde-json) which would handle the EOF checking and juggling of the deserializer for you. For serde_json I would like to focus on providing the foundational pieces to make something like that possible.

reviews.body: Impl looks good to me. Needs tests. API-wise, we need comments from potential users.

pr.title: Expose number of bytes processed by StreamDeserializer
